packages.description: aovine is a malicious crate (all published versions) identified as part of the same August 2026 crates.io supply-chain attack per the Rust Blog security advisory. The crate has been removed entirely from crates.io, so no version list is available.

append-only-vec 0.1.9 was published under the same compromised owner account and at the same time as the malicious arrayref 0.3.10 release, as part of the same crates.io supply-chain attack. ~4,484,606 downloads.

arrayref 0.3.10, published on crates.io by the arrayref owner account (presumably compromised), adds a first-ever dependency on the malicious typosquat package proc-macro1 1.0.107. Versions 0.3.5-0.3.9 were yanked under the same account to push cargo's 'consider updating to a version that is not yanked' warning toward the malicious 0.3.10. Reaches tiny-skia -> sctk-adwaita -> winit, affecting most Rust GUI tooling (egui/eframe, iced). arrayref <=0.3.9 remain clean.
proc-macro-en 1.0.10 is a malicious dependency published as part of the same August 2026 crates.io supply-chain attack as proc-macro1 and arrayref.

tinymember is a malicious crate (all published versions) identified as part of the same August 2026 crates.io supply-chain attack per the Rust Blog security advisory. The crate has been removed entirely from crates.io, so no version list is available.

arone is a malicious crate (all published versions) identified as part of the same August 2026 crates.io supply-chain attack per the Rust Blog security advisory. The crate has been removed entirely from crates.io, so no version list is available.

aronenao is a malicious crate (all published versions) identified as part of the same August 2026 crates.io supply-chain attack per the Rust Blog security advisory. The crate has been removed entirely from crates.io, so no version list is available.

internment 0.8.7 was published as part of the same August 2026 crates.io supply-chain attack as arrayref and proc-macro1; per the Rust Blog security advisory it was live for ~90 minutes (07:34-09:04 UTC) before removal. The crate has 14.4M all-time downloads; 0.8.6 and earlier remain clean.

proc-macro1 1.0.107 is a typosquat of proc-macro2 (source is a genuine copy, so builds succeed normally) with a malicious build.rs that downloads and executes a remote binary from 23.254.165.112:9089 (C2 at 23.254.165.112:443, passed as argv[1]), using a rustls ServerCertVerifier that unconditionally accepts all certificates. On Unix it drops to /tmp/rust-setup and spawns detached; on Windows it drops rust-setup.ps1 launched via a rust-setup-launch.vbs wrapper under wscript.exe, escaping cargo's job object via std::mem::forget. Package metadata forges authorship as David Tolnay with a repository URL that 404s.
